dedupe_keys.name: pyrorl reinforcement learning environment for wildfire evacuation

description: PyroRL is a simulation environment in which reinforcement learning agents learn when and by which routes to evacuate populated areas as a wildfire spreads across a grid. The producer is the Stanford Intelligent Systems Laboratory, and the environment is described in the Journal of Open Source Software (2024). Coverage is generic: users define the grid size, where people live, the evacuation paths and which areas may use them, so no particular region is built in. At each step the environment advances the fire, applies the agent's choice to evacuate an area along a path, closes paths that burn and returns a reward, with rendered animations of each episode. The code is available on GitHub and on PyPI (as pyrorl, earlier wildfire-evac) under the free MIT licence, with documentation and examples. Caveats: fire spread is a simple stochastic grid process, not a physical fire model, traffic congestion on paths is not represented, and the scenarios are synthetic unless users map real communities onto the grid. Simulation uses: training and comparing evacuation decision policies, teaching emergency managers how timing and route closure interact, and a test bed for coupling with detailed fire spread models. Related records: ELMFIRE (model-elmfire) and Cell2Fire (model-cell2fire) simulate fire spread physically, and JuPedSim (model-jupedsim) models pedestrian evacuation in detail.
inputs: Evacuation paths and which areas may use them
name: PyroRL: reinforcement learning environment for wildfire evacuation
outputs: Stepwise grid states of fire, populated cells and paths
provider: Stanford Intelligent Systems Laboratory (Joseph Guman, Joseph C. O'Brien, Christopher Pondoc and Mykel J. Kochenderfer)
